assumptions: steady state; Faraday's law: extent = current efficiency x N x I / (n F), F = 96485.33212 C/mol (CODATA 2018)
specified performance: cell voltage and current efficiencies are inputs; no polarisation curve, Nernst or Butler-Volmer model (no predictive electrochemistry)
current not assigned to a reaction (1 - FE - side fractions) causes no net chemical change (recombination of crossed-over products, shunt currents): its electricity becomes heat

isothermal boundary: feeds and products at the temperature of the heats of reaction; Q = P - sum(extent x dH); electricity counted once, as the DC power at the cell terminals (rectifier, transformer and busbar losses are outside the cell)
crossover and purge divide the formed products between outlets; they do not change the extents (no further reaction of a crossed-over product)
limitations: electrolyte properties (activities, heats of dilution, conductivity) are not modelled: the heats of reaction are those of process/reactions.yaml, on their own standard states (a linked dependency on electrolyte thermodynamics)
no adiabatic boundary, temperature rise or stream enthalpies (v1)

one current efficiency for the overall reaction: below 1 it reduces every product alike, and the current lost is heat, not chemistry; in a chlor-alkali cell the cathode forms H2 at about 100 % while hydroxide back-migration forms hypochlorite, chlorate and O2 (EU BREF 2014, 1.4.2: 1.070-1.128 t NaOH/t Cl2), so H2 and NaOH below a current efficiency of 1 are approximate (the electricity per t Cl2 is not affected); declare side reactions with their current fractions to include them
no polarisation curve: a voltage or efficiency outside the declared operating range is flagged, never extrapolated
not a unit of the DWSIM simulation (process/simulation.yaml): a linked flowsheet step is balanced with the cell's specified values

qualified.case: water electrolysis, H2O(l) -> H2 + 1/2 O2, n = 2 (PEM half-reactions)
qualified.checks: thermoneutral voltage from CODATA dfH(H2O, l); electricity per kg H2 against the US DOE PEM stack targets at 1.9, 1.8 and 1.6 V (rounded to 1 kWh/kg); at U_tn the electricity per kg equals the HHV of H2 and Q = 0
qualified.range: 1.6-1.9 V per cell, current efficiency 0.975-1, enthalpy basis 298.15 K

qualified.case: chlor-alkali membrane cell, 2 NaCl + 2 H2O -> Cl2 + H2 + 2 NaOH, n = 2
qualified.checks: thermoneutral voltage from CODATA ion enthalpies (infinite dilution); products per t Cl2 against the EU BREF's electrochemical unit (1.128 t NaOH, 28 kg H2); electricity per t Cl2 at 3.0 V and 95 % against the BREF's bipolar membrane range
qualified.range: 3.0 V at 6 kA/m2, current efficiency 0.95, enthalpy basis 298.15 K

sources: DOE PEM stack 2022 status: 1.9 V per cell
ideal current efficiency; reproduces the DOE PEM stack kWh/kg, whose footnote e nevertheless states a 2.5 % H2 crossover loss

findings.hint: give provenance: given with the source (measured, vendor or literature data)
